content: When resolving a ticket or issue, mark its status (`complete` / `resolved`) in the same commit as the code that satisfies it. If a code change lands separately from the ledger update, the ledger drifts: `storybloq_recommend` surfaces already-done work, wastes triage cycles, and can trigger fixes for problems that no longer exist. Before starting new work from the recommend list, verify each candidate against `git log --oneline` for merged PRs it might already reflect.
context: Session on 2026-09-06 opened with T-001 (preview isolation) marked inprogress though its fix had shipped in PR #6 (64b55bf), and ISS-009 (build broken) filed against a state that PR #9 (c4ffdb2) had already resolved before the finding was verified. Reconciliation took ~10 min of git-log correlation to sort out. Also observed: my own initial commit for ISS-004 accidentally bundled the pending .story/ scaffold + an untracked script because I ran `git add <paths>` on top of a pre-staged index instead of `git commit -- <paths>`. Root causes: (a) ticket status was left inprogress after the merge instead of being flipped complete in the commit, (b) staging state at session start wasn't verified before adding paths.
title: Update ticket/issue status in the same commit as the code change
